subject: Media Literacy
title: Satellite TV and the Global Village
description: A fast breakdown of Satellite TV and the Global Village for builders.

hook.text: In 1969, 600 million people watched the moon landing live on TV. The world shared one moment.

buildup.text: Satellite television turned local broadcasts into global ones, creating a shared media experience.

discovery.text: Marshall McLuhan called it the 'global village' — media was connecting all of humanity.

twist.text: But global media meant American and European content dominated, drowning out local voices.

climax.text: The global village had a megaphone — and only a few countries were holding it.

punchline.text: The village was global. The microphone was not.

quiz.question: What was a downside of satellite TV's global reach?
options: It was too expensive for anyone
Western content dominated and drowned out local voices
